facts: On the unit circle, $\tan\theta$ is the gradient of the radius $OP$: gradient $=\dfrac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}=\dfrac{y}{x}$.
This agrees with the right-triangle ratio: $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\dfrac{\text{opp}/\text{hyp}}{\text{adj}/\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}=\tan\theta$.
$\tan\theta$ is **undefined** when $\cos\theta=0$, at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and $\theta=270^{\circ}$, because you cannot divide by $0$.

foundation.question_text:
For which angles in $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$ is $\tan\theta$ undefined?
Explain why.
foundation.solution_text:
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ is undefined when $\cos\theta=0$.
On the unit circle $\cos\theta$ (the $x$-coordinate) is $0$ at the top and bottom, $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and $\theta=270^{\circ}$.
So $\tan\theta$ is undefined at $90^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}$.

foundation.question_text:
A point on the unit circle is $P(0.8,0.6)$.
Show that the gradient of $OP$ equals $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.
foundation.solution_text:
Gradient of $OP=\dfrac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}=\dfrac{0.6}{0.8}=0.75$.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\dfrac{0.6}{0.8}=0.75$
Both equal $0.75$, so the gradient of $OP$ equals $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.

development.question_text: Explain, using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$, why $\tan90^{\circ}$ is undefined but $\tan0^{\circ}$ is not.
development.solution_text:
At $90^{\circ}$, $P=(0,1)$, so $\cos90^{\circ}=0$ and $\tan90^{\circ}=\dfrac{1}{0}$, which is undefined.
At $0^{\circ}$, $P=(1,0)$, so $\cos0^{\circ}=1$ and $\tan0^{\circ}=\dfrac{0}{1}=0$.
Dividing by $0$ is undefined, but dividing $0$ by a non-zero number gives $0$.

development.question_text:
The point $P(0.28,0.96)$ lies on the unit circle.
Verify that the gradient of $OP$ equals $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.
development.solution_text:
Gradient of $OP=\dfrac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}=\dfrac{0.96}{0.28}=\dfrac{24}{7}$.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\dfrac{0.96}{0.28}=\dfrac{24}{7}$
Both equal $\dfrac{24}{7}$, so the gradient of $OP$ equals $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.

development.question_text: List all angles in $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$ where $\tan\theta$ is undefined, and state the reason in terms of $\cos\theta$.
development.solution_text:
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ is undefined exactly where $\cos\theta=0$.
On the unit circle $\cos\theta=0$ at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and $\theta=270^{\circ}$.
So $\tan\theta$ is undefined at $90^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}$.

mastery.question_text: Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$, explain why $\tan180^{\circ}$ is defined and equals $0$, but $\tan270^{\circ}$ is undefined.
mastery.solution_text:
At $180^{\circ}$, $P=(-1,0)$, so $\sin180^{\circ}=0$ and $\cos180^{\circ}=-1$.
$\tan180^{\circ}=\dfrac{0}{-1}=0$
At $270^{\circ}$, $P=(0,-1)$, so $\cos270^{\circ}=0$.
$\tan270^{\circ}=\dfrac{-1}{0}$, which is undefined because dividing by $0$ is undefined.
